title: Inventory of Lean Surface and Theorem Families

canonical_node.axiom: The inventory file is a reader-facing map of the current Lean surface, listing core files, theorem families, integrity markers, and the strong-law mechanism layer.
definitions: Core files: the listed Lean files that constitute the formal surface.
Theorem families: the listed groups of theorems and their associated properties.
Integrity markers: compact checkpoints that compile to indicate bundle coherence.
Strong-law mechanism layer: the file Theophysics_LawMechanisms.lean and its gates (GGate, MGate, FGate, CGate).
derivation: The document enumerates core files and their roles.
It identifies integrity markers as checkpoints.
It describes the strong-law mechanism layer and its gates.
canonical_node.action: The system should treat this inventory as a map for navigation and as a checklist for verifying that the listed files and markers exist and compile.
boundary: This document does not itself prove any theorem.
It does not define the semantics of the gates beyond naming them.
It does not assert that the listed theorems are true, only that they are part of the surface.
test: Check that each listed file exists in the repository.
Check that each listed marker theorem compiles.
Check that the listed theorem families are present in the corresponding files.

dg1_dependencies: The listed Lean files and their contents.
The marker theorems named in the document.
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a navigational map and a checklist for the Lean surface, enabling quick identification of files and theorem families.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the existence and role of the listed files and markers as a floor for further development.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this inventory, readers lose a structured overview, but the underlying Lean files remain; the map itself is not load-bearing for theorem correctness.

overstatement_risks: Treating the inventory as a proof of the theorems it lists.
Assuming the gates (GGate, MGate, FGate, CGate) have formal definitions beyond their naming.
Assuming the marker theorems are sufficient for correctness.
kill_conditions: If any listed file is missing or does not compile, the inventory becomes stale.
If the marker theorems are removed, the inventory's integrity checkpoints fail.
risk.lean_target: The inventory itself is not a Lean target; it is a map. The Lean targets are the listed files and markers.

plain_summary: This document is an inventory of the Lean formalization surface, listing core files, theorem families, integrity markers, and a strong-law mechanism layer. It serves as a navigational map and checklist, but does not itself prove any theorems.
